subject: pumpkin toadlet
title: This Frog Jumps Fine and Crash-Lands Almost Every Time

scenes.text: This frog can jump. It just can't land.
The pumpkin toadlet from Brazil is about one centimetre long, smaller than your thumbnail.
Filmed in slow motion, it spins in the air and smacks into the ground on its back or face.
Scientists scanned its head. Its balance organs are the smallest found in any adult vertebrate.
In tubes that tiny, the fluid barely moves, so its brain never feels the spin.
It shrank so far, it lost its sense of falling. It still jumps anyway.

description:
A 2022 study in Science Advances filmed Brazilian pumpkin toadlets (Brachycephalus) jumping and found most landings were uncontrolled crashes. Their inner-ear semicircular canals are the smallest known in any adult vertebrate, too small for the fluid inside to sense rotation properly.
The frogs are about one centimetre long.
Could you tell up from down with an inner ear that small?
first_comment: Their bright orange skin warns predators they're toxic, so a clumsy landing isn't fatal. What's the clumsiest animal you know?
